doc.title: Phil Woods interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999

title: Miles Davis's boost for his first Prestige record
summary: Woods credits Miles Davis with praising him to Prestige's Bob Weinstock.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Let me mention a couple of other musicians that you may have rubbed elbows with, and what’s your impression.

Always right next to me. Always very kind. Yeah in fact Miles is probably more responsible for my career than a lot of people realize. When I first signed with Prestige and I just did my first record Miles came by the office to see Bob Weinstock about something and Bob had a mock-up of the cover of my first record. And Miles said, “heard that guy at Birdland last night, he can play.” Now Bob Weinstock — Miles Davis is saying to the owner of the company that I can play? Who knows what might have gone on if Miles had not given me that little boost. And as I say he was always very kind. I never had any problem with Miles.
